Will an EcoFlow STREAM Ultra run a laptop computer? (EU)

Yes, it runs it — no usable-capacity figure see why below ↓

Every check passes: 5.2 W running against 1,200 W continuous. What this page will not do is turn a nameplate watt-hour rating into hours — see the evidence below for why.

Official spec + Derived by WattPair · verified 2026-08-01 · EU unit × laptop computer

Nominal capacity 1,920 Wh
Surge headroom 10×+

Two numbers decide this, and readers arrive using them interchangeably. Watts are the ceiling on what the inverter can hold at any instant — a laptop computer needs 5.2 W of them while it runs. Watt-hours are how much energy the battery holds, and the EcoFlow STREAM Ultra holds 1,920 Wh of them on the nameplate. A machine can have plenty of one and not enough of the other.

The verdict above is a calculation — running watts, start-up inrush and inverter waveform against this machine's continuous output and surge ceiling — not a lookup. What it will not do is print a runtime, and the reason is specific: EcoFlow publishes no depth of discharge or inverter efficiency for this model, so there is no usable-capacity figure to divide.

Where those numbers come from

Every figure below carries the tier it came from and the date it was checked. A blank is never left blank: a field the manufacturer does not publish says so, and a field whose sources disagree — two documents, or one document with itself — says that instead of picking one.

No usable-capacity figure for this machine

EcoFlow publishes a nameplate watt-hour number and nothing about depth of discharge or inverter efficiency for this model. Dividing the nameplate by this load would be wrong by 20–35% in the flattering direction, so this page shows the nameplate for what it is and refuses to turn it into hours.

Missing: station.usable_capacity_wh

The surge ceiling on this page is ours, not the manufacturer’s

EcoFlow does not publish a surge rating for this model. So the start-up check runs against the continuous output instead — an inverter cannot surge below what it sustains, which makes that the safest number we can defend. Real inverters usually manage 1.5–2× their continuous rating, so a start-up call held back by this figure may well be fine in practice; we are not going to say so until the manufacturer does.

Energy rate instead of a runtime

5.2 Wh per hour averaged over this load’s duty cycle

This number needs no battery figure at all, which is why this page can give it when it cannot give hours. Divide any usable-capacity figure you trust by it and you have your own runtime, with our arithmetic visible instead of hidden.

What a laptop computer demands

Running power 5.2 W Official spec · verified 2026-08-01 · high confidence
Start-up demand 5,750 W Official spec · verified 2026-08-01 · low confidence

This figure is on the record and it is deliberately not what the verdict was checked against: the spike lasts 50 ms — a capacitor charging, not a motor starting — while a station's surge rating describes a second-scale event. The two are not the same quantity, so the engine held this load's steady draw against the ceiling instead, 5.2 W. A site that compared them would fail this load against machines that run it perfectly well.

Questions people ask about this pairing

Will an EcoFlow STREAM Ultra run a laptop computer?
Yes. 5.2 W of running draw against 1,200 W of continuous output — 0.4% of it. The verdict is computed from running watts, start-up inrush and inverter waveform — the working is in the evidence section above.
How long will an EcoFlow STREAM Ultra run a laptop computer?
We will not put a number on it, and that is a finding rather than a gap. EcoFlow publishes no depth of discharge and no inverter efficiency for this model — only a nameplate watt-hour rating. Dividing that nameplate by this load produces a figure that is typically 20–35% too high while looking exactly as authoritative as a real one. What this page gives instead is the load's energy rate in watt-hours per hour, which needs no battery figure at all.
Where does the surge ceiling for the EcoFlow STREAM Ultra come from?
From us, and the page says so every time it uses it. EcoFlow publishes no surge rating for this model, so the start-up check runs against the continuous output as a conservative floor — an inverter cannot surge below what it sustains. Real inverters usually manage 1.5–2× their continuous rating, which means a start-up call held back by this figure may well be fine in practice. We will not say so until the manufacturer publishes a number.
